newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse charges ahead, could stabilise.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse charges ahead, could stabilise.

text.p: The Brussels leading Bel-20 share index closed at a new all-time high on Friday, shrugging off inflation worries in the U.S. following U.S. employment data which showed better-than-expected non-farm payroll figures.
Dealers were mixed over whether the Bel-20 would rise further in the coming week.
"We will stabilise after this rise, stocks are getting really expensive," said one trader.
The blue-chip Bel-20 index jumped to a record close, up 0.85 percent, or 16.37 points, to 1,945.99.
Analyst Gert De Mesure at Bank Delen said the index could go higher in the coming week as European fundamentals looked well placed.
"The Bel-20 is holding on well...there are some guys building up positions in selected Bel-20 stocks, like in Solvay, Royale Belge and Delhaize," De Mesure said.
Others were more cautious. "The levels are really high, I'm remaining cautious for Monday's session," said one trader at a major Belgian bank.
Dealers said one of the reasons for today's sharp rise was because a large brokerage house was executing major buying orders for foreign investors.
Cyclical stocks rallied today with chemicals firm Solvay climbing 3.52 percent to 20,600 francs.
Dealers said confidence in the pharmaceutical activities of the company and investors shopping around for stocks that had lagged recent bourse rises was attracting more investors to buy the stock.

"Technically we have passed an important resistance level (of around 19,500) in Solvay shares and everybody is confident of its pharmaceutical operations," said analyst Patrick Millecam at brokerage Corluy and Co.
Retailer Delhaize rose 1.53 percent to 1,985 francs after investors were confident the company would announce improved 1996 results.
Delhaize said after the bourse closed that it expected consolidated profit to be 15 to 20 percent higher in 1996 than in the previous year, it also expected to pay a higher dividend.
Elsewhere insurer Royale Belge shot up 3.44 percent to close at 6,920 francs.
"The stock was lagging behind compared to Fortis," said one trader.
Another trader said there was some arbitrage between insurer Fortis AG and Royale Belge following Fortis' recent gains.
"It (Royale Belge) is by no means a quality stock, it's only catching up with other stocks," said one trader at a major Belgian bank.
Fortis closed up 0.56 percent at 5,340 francs.
